narrative: Two employees were working on an empty above-ground 2,500-barrel crude oil tank. Employee 1 was welding while employee 2 was watching. Employee 1 saw fire behind the welding smoke and notified employee 2. Before they could get off the tank, they both fell in the tank and sustained burns from the fire.

An employee was retrieving material from the open bin of a digger derrick when the digger derrick contacted 7,200-volt primary electric lines. The employee sustained an electrical shock that went through his arms and exited his right foot.

While adjusting the ultra-high-pressure water blasting equipment in close proximity to normally energized cable 
trays, in three separate instances, two workers reported experiencing electrical shock sensations upon contacting 
the cable trays.
An employee was setting pipes on the ground and working on pipe support. The ground fell out, causing the pipes to slip and crush the employee's right leg.
An employee was loading out components of a stacked drilling rig when a beam flipped over and struck the employee. The employee suffered a broken leg and fractured ribs.
An employee was using a cutting torch to heat up bolts that had seized up. The bolts caught on fire in a flash burn, and the employee suffered burns to the arms and elbows.

At approximately 11:50 AM, a gas release was observed in the vicinity. The incident was reported by the surfer boat 
Captain who observed visible gas bubbles breaking the sea surface along the pipelines route. 
Subsea team started a sonar survey to locate any abnormalities on the gas lines in the area. The Subsea team 
widened the survey area and focused on 8” gas line and detected a gas release from this line which was confirmed 
to be the source of the observed bubbling.

Crude oil leak from a line coming from T-Junction and going central processing unit. The line was isolated. The 
total volume spilled is 10 bbls.

An employee was completing a fluid treatment process. The employee had just closed a 4-inch valve on a "T" manifold when he tripped and fell forward, striking the shin of his right leg against a valve handle and then landing on the ground. The employee's right leg sustained a spiral fracture requiring hospitalization and surgery.
An employee was detaching a 200-pound bale at or near an oil well site. He tripped on a rock and fell backward and the bale fell on his abdomen, causing internal bleeding.

An employee was bleeding down injection lines, using a 36-inch pipe wrench, to let hydrates thaw overnight. A valve was opened and pressure (about 900 psi) was released, causing a section of pipe to come loose and strike the employee's leg above the knee. He was hospitalized.
Fire on Oct 3, 2025; wells shut in and fire extinguished without injuries.
PLC programming loss prevented alarms/shut-ins, causing overflow; inlet shut manually and remediation started.

Incident 1: A threaded test port for a pressure relief valve on a compressor system failed due to fatigue induced by 
vibration.
During routine maintenance of the bonnet end cap on a blowout preventer, the cap fell and smashed an employee's right ring finger against another ram bonnet. The finger was amputated.
An employee was run over by a telehandler. The employee suffered a broken pelvis and was hospitalized.

Discharge line that had a 1” riser with a 1” ball valve was accidentally run over. Upon striking the riser, it broke off, 
and gas began to release.

An operator was removing a grating panel with manual handling hooks on the weather deck. 
During the operation, the grating unhooked from the manual handling tools and fell through the opening, hit a cable 
gate before landing on the underlying deck, approximately 10 meters below. The grating measures 1x1 meter and 
weighs 52,4 kg which gives a kinetic energy of 5149, 44 Joules. No one was injured, but under slightly changed 
circumstances people could have been in the line of fire as the deck was not cordoned off and there was a work 
team close to the area where it dropped.
Oil hauler failed to check his truck before loading and spilled.
On May 2, 2024, an employee was dumping a hopper into a bigger dumpster when his left ring finger got caught by the hopper and was amputated.

An employee was retrieving boxes from the roof of an interior lab/office. The employee fell through the roof approximately 10 feet to the floor below. The employee suffered a fractured left femur and patella as well as head lacerations.

During maintenance work at a Generation Unit, the mechanical technician suffered a fall from height, falling to a 
lower level from the engine access platform.
An employee fell from the top of a trailer loaded with bundles of tubes. He landed on the concrete walking surface 61 inches below, breaking two ribs and suffering shoulder, back, and lung injuries.

An employee was signaling a forklift operator as a 20-foot-long, 4-inch-thick section of steel pipe was lowered. The pipe came loose and fell striking the employee's head and shoulder. The employee sustained a head laceration and fractured ribs.

An employee was attempting to close a manual valve after flushing a hydraulic choke. When the manual valve would not close, he went to retrieve a tool (wrench) to help close the valve and tripped over a flow line. He fell to the ground and broke his left arm.
Employees were engaging in horseplay when the injured employee lost his balance and fell from the back of a digger derrick truck to the ground. The employee's leg was fractured in two places.

An employee was replacing a seized gearbox on an oil well using a breaker bar. After the breaker bar broke the gearbox loose, the bar struck the employee in the face, causing a fractured nasal bone and a laceration from the crown of the nose to above the right eye. The employee was hospitalized.
An employee was unpacking boxes at a receiving table. The employee tripped on a cable that had dropped off the table and fell, suffering a broken hip. The employee was hospitalized.
An employee was walking across a concrete parking lot when they slipped and fell on a patch of ice, resulting in a fractured leg.

An employee was replacing the well house. After installing the new well house, the employee drilled a 2- to 3-inch hole in the side of the well house to run a 2-inch pipe. The employee inserted the pipe into the hole and secured it inside the well house. The employee then traveled outside the well house to apply tape onto the threaded section of the new pipe. The employee used his left index finger to hold the tape on the threads. The pipe section inside the well house fell from its support and the employee's finger was lacerated, resulting in a fingertip amputation.
An employee was hospitalized after sustaining an electrical shock while unscrewing a light bulb on a training rig.
While performing well servicing operations, an employee became lightheaded and began vomiting. He was hospitalized for dehydration.

An employee was watching the landing joint being lowered into the rotary table when it clipped the slip bowl, causing the slip bowl to flip over and strike the employee's legs. The employee's right femur was fractured and they sustained a fracture to the left leg below the knee. The employee was hospitalized.
An employee was on a 4-foot podium ladder when the wind blew it over. He fell, and his left middle fingertip was amputated.
An employee suffered heat exhaustion and was given IV fluids. The employee was kept in the hospital for observation.
An employee was repairing a meter run and began to experience cramping. The employee was hospitalized for heat exhaustion.
An employee was performing maintenance on a forklift when they fell approximately 2 feet off the forklift and landed on a tote, resulting in multiple fractured ribs.

On July 17, 2015, at approximately 1:45pm, an employee was hospitalized after suffering two broken bones to his lower left leg. While applying pressure to the wrench, a reducer on the wrench broke, causing the employee to lose his balance. As he stepped down 34" to the gravel surface, he landed awkwardly on his left foot, causing fractures.

An employee was ventilating a building containing a gas leak and the gases ignited when the employee opened the door. The employee suffered first degree burns to the face and neck and second degree burns to both hands.
An employee was starting a pressure washer when a plug from the block valve blew out and struck the employee in the face, fracturing the left cheek and jaw.

An employee was adjusting the high/low switch on his truck-mounted welder. He was turning around when he lost his footing because it had just rained and his truck bed was slick. He went to steady himself and reached to grab onto something with his hands. His right hand slid underneath the cowling of his welder and two fingers were severely lacerated by the motor fan blades. He was hospitalized.
Flammable hydrocarbon released due to 30-LT0012A (1/2inch nipple) detached.

An employee was delivering a load to a customer location. As the employee made a right-hand turn onto a road, the tractor trailer tracked off the roadway and overturned. The employee sustained bleeding on the brain, a fractured collarbone, and a fractured finger.

At the facility shop area, an employee tripped over his feet and fell on an industrial sized valve stem used in hydrofracking (a piece of sharp equipment) and lacerated his abdomen. This injury required hospitalization for two days.

downhole guides on the upper deck level, but one down hole guide clamp, weighing 7 kg, slipped and dropped

the IP to fall on to the grating resulting in bruises to his right forehead and injury to his right knee.
A gas leak occurred as a result of a crack in a nipple on the 4-inch line associated with the globe valve.

A trailer driver was transporting six concrete barriers (3.5t each) on a flatbed trailer. The barriers were stacked in 
two rows (three in each row), with one cargo lashing belt securing two concrete barriers each. While the trailer was

Fortunately, no injuries or damage occurred.
During fibre optic installation work, an 8” pipe was broken by a backhoe excavator.

Operator noticed that the tap was in the open position. Release had overflowed onto the building floor. Small

Gas release occurred from 8” blinded flange on TEG contactor due to the degradation of incorrect designed rubber 
gasket left installed.

An employee was opening the top steam vent on the main fractionator. The trapped hot condensate from the vent leaked out and landed on the employee's back and shoulders. The employee was hospitalized with second degree burns.

An employee was conducting work on the 60-feet-high platform of an oil derrick, operating rigging to move piping into position. The employee became sick, vomited, experienced cramps, and was eventually hospitalized for heat-related health issues.

An employee fell from a tractor and struck her head on the ground, resulting in a concussion. She was hospitalized overnight.

An employee was walking along a narrow rural roadway toward the back of a digger derrick truck as another digger derrick truck was moving forward from the opposite direction, passing the parked vehicle. The employee's foot was run over by the tire of the vehicle. The employee sustained fractures to the top of the right foot and a dislocated big toe.

During the breaking of a connection, an employee was holding a "mud bucket" against a pipe to minimize the splashing of mud on an oil rig floor. A crew of five employees used two forklifts along with a telehandler to load and carry pipe that had been cut into 125-foot sections from the fuel pier to the parking lot for painting. The injured employee was guiding the pipe while it was being moved by the forklift. An incident occurred during the transfer of an amine solution from a truck to a storage tank. The transfer 
was performed using a corrugated flexible hose connected to the truck with a threaded coupling and to the 
tank with a metal clamp. The end of the transfer was verified by observing hose vibrations generated during 
nitrogen displacement operations. After completing the transfer, one operator closed the nitrogen valve used for 
pressurization toward the truck and visually confirmed closure of the amine discharge valve on the truck. The 
second operator entered the containment area to close the tank valves. After closing the needle valve located near 
the tank, while attempting to close the ball valve, the hose suddenly detached from the nozzle, causing an amine 
splash that hit the operator’s face through a gap between the visor and the chin. While attempting to wash at the 
eyewash station, the operator rubbed his face and eyes with contaminated hands, worsening the injury. He was 
immediately assisted by a colleague, taken to the infirmary, and then transported to the emergency room.
Bottom valve sand blockage masked fluid level, releasing 43 bbl oil during manway opening; no injuries.

On Thursday March 13th, 2025, the crew change bus had a road accident. It was 18h30 and after a heavy rain at the 
time of the incident.
The bus driver was driving too close to the road edge to avoid potholes of the road section. While doing so a part of 
the road edge collapsed under the right front bus tire making the bus end its trajectory on the pipelines on the side

Immediate action:

• The TAG removed.

A Mechanic and an E-Tech were repairing a section of the natural gas manifold on frac pump. The employees were 
replacing a section on the manifold referred to as a pistol. After the repairs were made the employees opened 
the natural gas supply valve to supply the gas manifold on the pump. The mechanic stepped up onto a platform to 
open the main ball valve of the natural gas manifold to allow the pump to start burning the natural gas as fuel. As 
the mechanic (IP) opened the main ball valve, both employees heard a loud pop noise. The top of the low-pressure 
regulator (VDR) broke away from its base and struck the mechanic in the head above his right eye causing a 
laceration. The top of the VDR is made of aluminum and weighs approximately 1lb/~454g. The IP was evaluated at a 
local emergency room, and the IP received 8 sutures to close the laceration.
An employee was walking into the dog house to warm up and closed the door on her hand resulting in a fractured right thumb.

A chemical operator was performing a transfer and dosing operation of a caustic product into a cooling water 
system in an industrial plant. During the disconnection of a hose used for product injection (in an improvised 
location), residual pressure caused the chemical to splash onto the operator’s face and over his protective coverall. 
In reaction, the operator jumped from a portable ladder (about 1.5 meters high), resulting in a twisted ankle in 
addition to the chemical burn. The worker received immediate first aid and required medical attention, leading to 
time off work.

During the dismantling of scaffolding in a 45° angular configuration, assembler 01 had to apply excessive force 
to loosen a remaining clamp (exposed to the weather) using a ratchet wrench, causing the bolt to shear and 
subsequently break. With the sudden opening of the clamp, the tube (3.65 kg) slipped from his left hand, fell, and 
slid along the structure, traveling a lateral distance of approximately 4.5 meters, striking the back of assembler 04s 
helmet on the lower level, resulting in a superficial cut to the scalp.

An employee was about to change out the choke parts to fix a leaking choke on the belly dump of a gas production unit (GPU). While the choke was being unbolted, pressure came through it, blowing the employee backward and causing lacerations and broken bones in their face.

An employee was acting as a spotter for the loading of a rig pump. The employee tried to remove a pin that was in the way of the resting point of the pump and his right thumb was caught in a pinch point, resulting in an amputation of the thumb at the first knuckle.
An employee was helping to load a truck. A pipe in the truck began shifting and he went to try to grab it when he fell backward to the ground and broke an arm.

Two employees were helping welders by holding a 16" flange when a flash fire occurred. The first employee suffered a puncture wound from a vent pipe and burns to the face. The second employee suffered burns to the back of his neck, his back, and his right arm.

An employee was driving an all-terrain vehicle to inspect a well. The vehicle struck an uneven surface, ejecting the employee from the vehicle to the ground. The employee sustained bilateral leg fractures.
An employee was opening the oil tank hatch when a spark ignited the material inside the tank. The employee sustained burns to the face, back and hands.

An employee was adjusting the operator console to raise it to a higher level. He removed the bracket that connects the console to the rail system so he could begin raising it. The console shifted, causing the employee to fall 10 feet, resulting in a shoulder fracture and head laceration.

Crews were performing flange management on the water 16’’ and 18’ lines and installation of the blind flange on 
the 24’ overboard line for hydrotest. During the process, crew encountered a clash with an abandoned open 18’ line 
and started hot cutting the 18’ line to make room to install a blind flange. Fire broke out at worksite, resulting in 17 
people injured (including first aid cases) and 1 person missing.

On 27 December at approximately 07:30, cleaning cloths contaminated with cooking oil were washed and dried in 
the laundry.

ventilation, exhaust, and air-conditioning systems were switched off while the room was unattended.
At approximately 13:15, the cloths began releasing smoke and an incipient fire developed. The steward used a dry 
chemical extinguisher and the fire brigade extinguished the fire.
No injuries or damage occurred, but the event had serious fire potential.

As the employees were loosening the bolts to open the pipe and placing the blind, a valve that was holding back the slurry opened. This released the hot slurry (640 degrees Fahrenheit) onto the employees performing the work. Both employees sustained thermal burns from the slurry and were hospitalized.
An employee was attaching a compressor to a skid with a pneumatic impact driver. The employee's finger got caught in the driver, which tore off his fingertip; the injury did not involve the bone.

An employee was pulling serial numbers off a hydraulic valve. The strap that was being used to hold the valve snapped and the valve fell, pinning the employee against a forklift. The employee suffered broken ribs and was hospitalized.
An employee was power washing the shop when he was struck by a reversing forklift that ran over and broke his right leg.

An employee was using a roustabout. As he was lowering the hook for the cable and pulling the slack out of it, the lift began to tip over. The employee went to move out of the way but tripped and fell in the process. The lift then fell on the employee, lacerating his left leg and abdomen.

Both employees were hospitalized.

While an employee was moving a small pile of hot material with a bobcat, a flash of steam entered the cab of the bobcat. The employee exited the cab and tripped into a pool of hot water, receiving first and second degree burns and requiring hospitalization.

During batch treatment on the flowline, a gas lift line was misidentified as the flowline. A bull plug was misidentified 
and opened.

An employee was using a pressure washer at an oil and gas site. The water pressure was approximately 1400 psi. He lost control of the hose and the wand struck the employee's left hand causing a laceration between the thumb and wrist. The employee was hospitalized overnight.
An employee was helping load a trailer. The vehicle was jostled and his left middle finger was crushed between the truck and the hitch. He suffered an amputation to the finger.

Two electricians were troubleshooting an HVAC (condenser) unit in a control room. Both employees went to the control room and applied group lockout to a single disconnect rated at 250 VDC power. After locking out the power to the control room and condenser unit, the employees began troubleshooting several deficiencies they observed while looking through the control panel. After repairing those items, the two employees removed the locks and validated that the repairs were working. The employees observed everything working as required except the HVAC compressor. The injured employee went up to the condenser area on an elevated walking surface that was covered in blaze which is a byproduct of the coke produced at the plant. The accumulation of blaze created an uneven surface. The employee had to remove an exterior covering or guard to validate that 250 VDC was coming from the thermostat to the junction box on the compressor motor. The employee squatted down and lost his balance before checking for 250 VDC. The employee reached to catch himself and in doing so grabbed the belts that drive the compressor motor. When contact was made, the motor began running and the employee's left hand was pulled through the pulleys amputating his left middle and ring fingers.

An employee was loading asphalt from a storage tank into a tanker truck from an above ground asphalt loading rack. After removing the loading spout from the tanker and placing a bucket drip pan under it, the employee stepped onto the crows nest of the truck to close the loading hatch. Residual asphalt (approximately 370 degrees F) in the loading line spilled out of the spout, into the bucket, and splashed down onto the employee below. The employee sustained second-degree burns to the back of his head, neck, ears, and side of his face near the jawline. The employee was hospitalized.
An employee suffered an amputation injury while rigging up a top drive at or near Parshall, North Dakota.
An employee was removing bolts from a wellhead tree when the tree fell onto his left leg, resulting in lower leg fractures.

At approximately 05:45, a rupture occurred in a gas lift riser pipeline. Gas detectors on the unit identified the 
presence of a gas cloud, which triggered an emergency shutdown of the facility, resulting in the immediate halt of 
production operations. Personnel were promptly relocated to designated muster points as a precautionary measure.
Firefighting and oil recovery vessels were deployed to the site for monitoring and response. An emergency response 
structure was mobilized at the operations center. A subsea construction vessel equipped with a remotely operated 
vehicle (ROV) was assigned to inspect the risers on the offshore platform to identify the source of the leak.
Continuous monitoring of gas sensors confirmed that the gas detection had ceased. The rupture in the gas lift riser 
is currently under investigation. Further laboratory analysis of the damaged riser is required to determine the root 
cause, and the event remains under investigation pending these results.

When filling a mud tank with brine to prepare for cleaning of the tank, the transfer hose became dislodged, fell

Achilles tendon. The operator required surgery, classifying this as a Lost Work Day Case under IOGP guidelines. The 
incident is considered high potential, as the heavy hose coupling could have caused a fatality if it struck the head of 
the injured person when it fell.

An employee was vacuuming catalyst inside a confined space. A piece of the catalyst rolled down from the pile and struck his leg, breaking the femur. He was hospitalized.

An employee was cleaning oil off the floor of a turbine unit with a pressure washer at a compressor station when he began to feel dizzy and later experienced headaches. He was hospitalized for heat exhaustion.
Operator observed oil spilling from tank.
